batch:
Survey's done and batch 1 is below. Nothing is recorded yet, and I haven't edited the estate.

**Current estate (arc-next inputs)**

| Kind | Count | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Rules | 80 active (57 with obligations, 23 prod-only), high-water T-85 | about 5 KB of rule text, 22 KB pin |
| Obligations | 59: 56 active, 1 waived, 1 deferred, 1 split parent | 60 KB, 57 KB rendered |
| Ledger | 39 entries | 2.7 KB |
| Debt | 15 open | 6.7 KB |

Phase 0 already omits T-81 to T-85, C-39 and I-54, so none of them need a decision.

**Problem outside compaction: most witnesses don't exist in this tree**
- 58 obligations name witness tests, and only I-20's test id exists in `test/register.test.js`. The file has three tests: `list`, `I-20` and `cancelled exports`.
- Those obligations still carry `proves` judgments, but SCHEMAS says a missing test holds no property.
- `src/` also has no code for dates, audit, slips, sessions, locks, tokens or the archive.
- I'm not proposing a fix here because this belongs in normal adjudication. It does affect the merges below: a merged witness has to be a real test, so I name the real test where one exists.

**Batch 1: overtaken rules, duplicates and low-value rules**

If you approve all ten, rules go from 80 to 66 and obligations from 59 to 53.

1. retire T-8
   - Items: T-8 "The PortLink SOAP bridge retries failed deliveries every ten minutes." and its obligation I-8.
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: the retry demand on a bridge that no longer exists. `src/` and `test/` have no trace of it.
   - Why: the previous arc removed the bridge.

2. retire T-33
   - Items: T-33 "Dispatch is allowed until 72 hours before the tide (working assumption P-1)." and its obligation I-33.
   - Replacement: none. T-72 "Dispatch is allowed until 48 hours before the tide." already records your P-1 answer.
   - Gives up: the 72-hour cutoff, and the only obligation on dispatch timing.
     - T-72 is prod-only, so no test will check the 48-hour cutoff after this. Testing it would be slice work.
     - Applying this also means changing P-1's `bears` from T-33 to T-72 and removing the T-33 sentence from the `register.md` prose.
   - Why: your answer replaced the assumption.

3. merge T-3 and T-14
   - Items: T-3 "A berth booking identifier is unique across the register." and T-14 "No two entries in the register have the same berth booking identifier."
   - Replacement: T-3, text unchanged. T-14 and I-14 go.
   - Gives up: nothing. Both demand one identifier per register, cancelled entries included, and `insert` checks every row.
     - I-3's witness must become a real test. The duplicate assertion currently sits in test `I-20`.
   - Why: they're the same rule in different words.

4. merge T-27 into T-41
   - Items: T-27 "The export command refuses invalid dates." and T-41 "Every command refuses invalid dates before reading or writing records."
   - Replacement: T-41, text unchanged. T-27 and I-27 go.
   - Gives up: nothing. T-41 covers export and adds an ordering demand.
     - I-41's witness must exercise export.
   - Why: T-41 fully covers T-27.

5. merge T-65, T-66, T-67, T-68, T-69 and T-71 into T-41
   - Items: "The {reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list, inspect} command validates dates before changing storage." All six are prod-only.
   - Replacement: T-41, text unchanged.
   - Gives up: one narrow property. "Storage" is wider than "records", so these six commands could write non-record storage, such as an audit line, before refusing a bad date. I'd accept that, since auditing a refused attempt seems reasonable.
     - If you want no loss, I'd use a new rule instead: T-? "Every command refuses invalid dates before reading records or changing storage." It would replace T-41 too, and I-41 would need a fresh proof.
   - Why: this removes six unwitnessed lines already nearly covered by a witnessed rule.

6. merge T-36 and T-37
   - Items: T-36 "The JSON export includes cancelled records." and T-37 "The CSV export includes cancelled records."
   - Replacement: T-? "The JSON and CSV exports include cancelled records."
   - Gives up: nothing, but a failure no longer points at one format from the obligation id alone.
     - I-36 re-anchors at rev 2 with a fresh proof, and I-37 goes.
     - The witness becomes the real `cancelled exports` test, which asserts both formats.
   - Why: they're one property with a single existing test.

7. tighten T-49
   - Items: T-49 "In order to ensure that the operator can rely on the output when things go wrong, every failed command, without exception, prints its diagnostic to stderr rather than to stdout."
   - Replacement: T-49 "Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, not stdout." The purpose moves to `register.md` prose: "Diagnostics stay off stdout so the operator can rely on the output when a command fails."
   - Gives up: nothing. I checked all three demands: every failure, stderr, and not stdout.
     - I-49 goes to rev 2 and needs a fresh proof.
   - Why: same meaning in under half the words.

8. retire T-52
   - Items: T-52 "Comment text is grammatical English." and I-52, whose statement has drifted to "One internal comment is grammatical English."
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: any requirement on comment grammar. `src/` has no comments today.
   - Why: it doesn't serve V-1 or V-2, yet it costs a must-hold obligation.

9. retire T-62
   - Items: T-62 "Internal local variable names use lower camel case." Prod-only.
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: the naming convention as a requirement. Current code conforms, but nothing would hold it there.
   - Why: this is style, not target behaviour.

10. retire T-63
    - Items: T-63 "The command must be implemented in executable program instructions." Prod-only.
    - Replacement: none.
    - Gives up: nothing observable, because no working command can violate it.
    - Why: it's vacuous.

**Leaving alone after checking**
- **T-20, I-20 and C-34:** this is the integrity boundary. F-1 and F-2 reproduced its failure, and I-20 is the one witness that really exists.
- **T-21 and I-21:** the next slice is built on them.
- **T-72:** it holds your P-1 answer.
- **C-31, C-32, I-55 and I-56:** the waiver and deferral are still live, so the sort family won't be merged across them.
- **I-59 and I-60:** these are children of I-58 under T-58, not obligations of T-59 and T-60. The matching numbers are a coincidence, so later merges of those rules won't touch them.

**Later batches**
- **Rule families:** merges that list each command explicitly rather than widening to "every command". This batch also includes retiring T-5 and T-6: `list` and `export` exit 0 with no id, which contradicts those rules, and the `list` test and README both rely on it.
- **Ledger:** folding the archive and token policies into the corpus, which also means updating the C-12 and C-38 citations in `slips.json`.
- **Debt:** resolving the remaining items.
- **If you approve everything:** roughly 25 rules, 21 obligations, 13 ledger entries and no open debt.

Which of these do you approve? "All", or numbers plus any changes, works. For 5, I recommend T-41 unchanged, accepting the named loss.
reply:
1: approve
2: approve
3: approve. Keep T-3's text unchanged.
4: approve
5: reject
6: reject. Keep T-36 and T-37 as they are.
7: approve, using this exact wording instead: "Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, never stdout." No `register.md` prose addition.
8: reject as written. Retire I-52 only, and keep T-52. The only loss I accept is the separate test demanding grammatical English in one internal comment.
9: approve
10: approve

batch:
Decisions 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 (I-52 only), 9 and 10 are recorded as K-1 to K-8 in `../roadmap-inputs/drafts/compaction.md`. Decisions 5 and 6 are rejected and won't come back, so rules are now at 74 and obligations at 54.

**A side effect of K-6:** I gave T-52 the census state `untestable`, which is where the orchestrate skill puts principles. The executor sends every `untestable` and `prod-only` rule to every unit (`src/holistic/impact.ts:87`), so T-52 now reaches every unit's rule set. That's one extra line per unit. It also means merging prod-only rules saves text on every unit, which is why decisions 2 and 3 below are worth doing.

**Batch 2: contradicted rules and command families**

If you approve all ten, rules go from 74 to 47 and obligations from 54 to 38.

Each merge lists its commands exactly and doesn't widen to commands the family never covered. Decisions 8, 9 and 10 have the same shape as the T-36/T-37 merge you rejected, so if you reject them for the same reason, I'll drop the remaining witnessed family merges without asking again.

1. retire T-70
   - Items: T-70 "The welcome banner ends with a period." Prod-only.
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: the punctuation demand on a banner the product doesn't have.
   - Why: it sends a line about a banner that doesn't exist to every unit.

2. merge T-73 to T-80
   - Items: "The {reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect, search} command leaves the previous file intact when a write fails." All eight are prod-only.
   - Replacement: T-? "Every command leaves the previous file intact when a write fails."
   - Gives up: nothing. The family already names all eight commands in `cli.js`. The new wording also binds any future command.
   - Why: this is eight lines to every unit for one property.

3. merge T-59, T-60, T-61 and T-64
   - Items: "The {arrive, depart, list, search} command returns exit 0 for an empty result." All four are prod-only.
   - Replacement: T-? "The arrive, depart, list and search commands return exit 0 for an empty result."
   - Gives up: nothing. T-57 and T-58 stay separate because they have live obligations, and I-59 and I-60 aren't touched.
     - This merge carries over an existing conflict. `search` with no match exits 2 today, which T-16 demands and T-64 appears to forbid. That needs adjudication either way.
   - Why: four lines with one meaning.

4. retire T-5
   - Items: T-5 "The list command rejects a missing record id with exit 2." and I-5.
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: any id requirement on `list`. I ran `list` with no id and it exits 0. The README and the `list` test both use that form.
   - Why: the product overtook the rule, and `list` doesn't take an id.

5. retire T-6
   - Items: T-6 "The export command rejects a missing record id with exit 2." and I-6.
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: any id requirement on `export`. I ran it with no id and it prints JSON and exits 0, because its first argument is the format.
   - Why: same as T-5.

6. retire T-13
   - Items: T-13 "The list command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage." and I-13.
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: rejection of an unknown id on `list`. `list nosuch` ignores the argument and exits 0, and it writes nothing.
   - Why: `list` has no id argument to reject.

7. retire T-9
   - Items: T-9 "The reserve command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage." and I-9.
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: the refusal itself, which can't coexist with how records are created. `reserve newid one morning` wrote a new record and exited 0.
     - Duplicate ids stay refused under T-3.
   - Why: a new id is what `reserve` is for.

8. merge T-1, T-2, T-4 and T-7
   - Items: "The {reserve, cancel, depart, inspect} command rejects a missing record id with exit 2." and I-1, I-2, I-4, I-7. This assumes decisions 4 and 5 pass; otherwise T-5 and T-6 stay outside this merge as their own rules.
   - Replacement: T-? "The reserve, cancel, depart and inspect commands each reject a missing record id with exit 2."
   - Gives up: per-command obligation ids, so a failure no longer identifies the command from the id alone. No demand is lost.
     - I-1 re-anchors at rev 2 with a fresh proof, and its witness needs one real test per command.
   - Why: this removes three obligations and three rule lines.

9. merge T-10, T-11, T-12, T-15 and T-16
   - Items: "The {cancel, arrive, depart, inspect, search} command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage." and I-10, I-11, I-12, I-15, I-16. This assumes decisions 6 and 7 pass.
   - Replacement: T-? "The cancel, arrive, depart, inspect and search commands each reject an unknown record id without writing storage."
   - Gives up: per-command obligation ids. No demand is lost.
     - I-10 re-anchors at rev 2 with a fresh proof, and its witness needs one real test per command.
   - Why: this removes four obligations and four rule lines.

10. merge T-17, T-18, T-19, T-22, T-23 and T-24
    - Items: "The {reserve, cancel, arrive, export, inspect, search} command prints the record id on successful completion." and I-17, I-18, I-19, I-22, I-23, I-24.
    - Replacement: T-? "The reserve, cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search commands each print the record id on successful completion."
    - Gives up: per-command obligation ids. No demand is lost.
      - I-17 re-anchors at rev 2 with a fresh proof, and its witness needs one real test per command.
    - Why: this removes five obligations and five rule lines.

**Still to come**
- **Next batch:** the operator-refusal, timestamp and audit families if you accept this merge shape, then the ledger folds and merges.
- **After that:** debt.

Which of these do you approve?

batch:
Only `slips.json` cites any of these entries, and only C-12 and C-38. This is the last batch. I've left out the session, lock, audit-directory, UTC and redaction ledger families. They're the same family merge you just rejected, and the ledger never reaches worker prompts, so the saving is only about 1.5 KB of root-facing text.

**Batch 3: ledger and debt**

If you approve all nine, rules go from 74 to 76, the ledger from 39 entries to 39 (six removed, up to four added for debt), and open debt from 15 to 0. New ledger ids start at C-41 and get assigned when I record.

1. fold C-4
   - Items: C-4 "The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision."
   - Replacement: T-? "The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision." Census state `out-of-slice`, since no archive code exists yet. C-4 leaves the ledger.
   - Gives up: nothing. I checked both demands, append-only and corrections as new revisions, and the text is unchanged. C-4 never had a witness, and nothing cites it.
   - Why: seats never see C-n text, so a standing truth belongs in the corpus.

2. fold C-12 and C-17
   - Items: C-12 "A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response." and C-17 "Retries with the same request token return the stored response without another mutation."
   - Replacement: T-? "A request token is accepted once; retries with the same request token return the stored response without another mutation." Census state `out-of-slice`, since no token code exists yet. Both entries leave the ledger.
   - Gives up: nothing. I checked accepted once, same-token retries, stored response and no second mutation.
     - `slips.json` cites C-12, so that citation has to go first. Removing it changes nothing for seats, because they never receive C-n text.
   - Why: the two entries overlap, and it's a standing policy that seats can't currently read.

3. retire C-23
   - Items: C-23 "The first release demo uses the blue harbour slide template."
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: the template choice for that demo. The cut line says the previous release is complete, and nothing cites C-23.
   - Why: its one occasion has passed.

4. retire C-30
   - Items: C-30 "Retire the old walkthrough obligation I-54."
   - Replacement: none.
   - Gives up: the ledger's note of why I-54 left. The `arc-previous` inputs and git history still hold it.
     - T-54 stays active as prod-only and C-31 and C-32 stay in force.
     - C-30 calls I-54 a walkthrough obligation, but I-54's statement was about export sorting. I can't explain that mismatch, so check it if the label means something to you.
   - Why: the disposition has landed, and I-54 is already gone from the arc-next inputs.

5. retire C-38
   - Items: C-38 "Temporary trace output is permitted for this arc only."
   - Replacement: none. C-40 "Trace output redacts operator credentials." stays.
   - Gives up: the permission for temporary trace output. The arc it covered is complete, and the product has no trace output.
     - `slips.json` cites C-38, so that citation has to go first. If the slip unit needs trace output, it would need a new ruling.
   - Why: its own text says it has expired.

6. resolve B-2
   - Items: B-2 "Remove the retry queue in the PortLink SOAP bridge."
   - Replacement: C-? "B-2 is closed: the previous arc removed the PortLink SOAP bridge and its retry queue."
   - Gives up: nothing. The work is done, and `src/` and `test/` have no trace of the bridge. This doesn't depend on T-8.
   - Why: obsolete.

7. resolve B-6
   - Items: B-6 "Index reserve record lookup; B-1 already tracks the same index."
   - Replacement: C-? "B-6 is closed as a duplicate of B-1."
   - Gives up: nothing. B-1 carries the same work.
   - Why: duplicate, by its own text.

8. resolve B-11
   - Items: B-11 "Align the success message punctuation with the help footer."
   - Replacement: C-? "B-11 is closed as negligible: success message punctuation need not align with the help footer."
   - Gives up: the alignment work. Any mismatch stays. Today a success prints only the id, and the code has no help footer.
   - Why: negligible.

9. resolve the index debt
   - Items, all "Add an index for {x} lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call.":
     - Record lookup: B-1 reserve, B-3 arrive, B-4 depart, B-5 list, B-7 inspect, B-8 search.
     - Audit lookup: B-9 reserve, B-10 cancel, B-12 depart, B-13 list, B-14 export, B-15 inspect.
   - Replacement: C-? "Register and audit lookup indexes are not demanded; commands may scan the local file. Reopen as new debt if register size makes scans a real cost."
   - Gives up: every planned index, so linear scans stay. Each command already parses the whole JSON file, so an index wouldn't avoid reading it. The audit trail these would index doesn't exist in the code yet.
     - If you approve 7 and reject 9, B-1 stays open and B-6 still closes.
   - Why: this is the largest debt group, and nothing in V-1 or V-2 depends on scan speed.
     - You could approve only the audit group or only the record group.

Which of these do you approve?
reply:
1: approve
2: approve with my wording: "A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response without another mutation."
3: approve
4: reject
5: reject
6: approve, no replacement entry needed
7: approve, no replacement entry needed; B-1 stays open
8: approve, no replacement entry needed
9: reject

Item 2: removing the C-12 citation from `slips.json` must not change T-21. Flag it if it does.
